description: Unix one-liners for bioinformatics — FASTQ / FASTA parsing, sequence search, awk / grep / sed, SAM, VCF, BED, GTF

cheats.title: Lines N to M of a file
Browse a wide table without wrapping
cheats.notes: Arrow keys scroll sideways, / searches, q quits

cheats.title: Search files recursively with line numbers
Show matches with 3 lines of context
Match a list of IDs from a file
cheats.notes: -F plain text (no regex), -w whole words, -f patterns from a file — fast for thousands of IDs

cheats.title: Find and replace in a file (macOS)
cheats.notes: On Linux / the HPC it's  sed -i 's/old/new/g' file  (no '')

cheats.title: Count each unique line, most common first
Pick columns (tab separated)
cheats.notes: For CSV:  cut -d, -f1,3

cheats.title: Print a column with awk
cheats.notes: Drop -F'\t' to split on any whitespace; use -F, for CSV

cheats.title: Keep rows where a column passes a cutoff (drop header)
cheats.notes: Without NR > 1 the header sneaks through, because awk compares text with numbers as strings

cheats.title: Keep the header, filter the rest
How many columns each line has
cheats.notes: Quick check for broken rows in a table

cheats.title: Lines in both files
cheats.notes: -23 = only in the first file, -13 = only in the second

cheats.title: Compare two files side by side
Look inside a .gz file
cheats.notes: On macOS zcat doesn't read .gz — use gzip -cd (works everywhere)

cheats.title: Checksums to verify a transfer
cheats.notes: md5 file on macOS, md5sum file on Linux — match against the provider's checksum list

cheats.title: Loop over files
cheats.cmd:
for f in *.{{ext:fastq.gz}}; do
  echo "$f"
done

cheats.title: Loop over R1 / R2 pairs
cheats.cmd:
for r1 in *_R1*.fastq.gz; do
  r2=${r1/_R1/_R2}
  echo "$r1  $r2"
done

cheats.title: Run on many files in parallel
Save output and errors to one log
Keep running after logout
cheats.notes: Or run it inside tmux

cheats.title: Find and kill a process
cheats.notes: Then  kill <PID>  (kill -9 <PID> if it won't stop)

cheats.title: Search your command history
cheats.cmd: Ctrl+R then type — Ctrl+R again for older matches

cheats.title: Command-line editing keys
cheats.cmd: Ctrl+A start · Ctrl+E end · Ctrl+U delete to start · Ctrl+W delete word · Alt+B / Alt+F word back / forward

cheats.title: Reuse the last command / last argument
cheats.notes: sudo !!  reruns the last command with sudo

cheats.title: Print only the sequences (every 4th line from line 2)
cheats.notes: NR%4==1 headers · ==2 sequences · ==3 '+' lines · ==0 qualities. Plain .fastq: awk 'NR%4==2' reads.fastq

cheats.title: One read per line (4 lines → 1 tab-separated)
cheats.notes: Handy for filtering whole reads with awk/grep, then  tr '\t' '\n'  to turn it back into FASTQ

cheats.title: Count reads containing a sequence
cheats.notes: AGATCGGAAGAGC is the Illumina adapter — a quick adapter check

cheats.title: Count a sequence on both strands
cheats.cmd:
s={{sequence}}; rc=$(echo $s | rev | tr ACGTacgt TGCAtgca)
gzip -cd {{reads.fastq.gz}} | awk 'NR % 4 == 2' | grep -cE "$s|$rc"

cheats.title: Pull out whole reads containing a sequence
cheats.cmd: gzip -cd {{reads.fastq.gz}} | paste - - - - | awk -F'\t' -v s={{sequence}} 'index($2, s)' | tr '\t' '\n' > {{hits.fastq}}

cheats.title: Pull out reads by name
cheats.notes: names.txt: one read name per line, with the leading @

cheats.title: Average read length
cheats.cmd: gzip -cd {{reads.fastq.gz}} | awk 'NR % 4 == 2 {s += length($0); n++} END {print s/n}'

cheats.title: GC content of all reads
cheats.cmd: gzip -cd {{reads.fastq.gz}} | awk 'NR % 4 == 2 {gc += gsub(/[GCgc]/, ""); at += gsub(/[ATat]/, "")} END {printf "%.2f%%\n", 100 * gc / (gc + at)}'

cheats.title: Length of every sequence
cheats.cmd: awk '/^>/ {if (name) print name "\t" len; name = substr($1, 2); len = 0; next} {len += length($0)} END {print name "\t" len}' {{file.fasta}}

cheats.title: Put each sequence on one line
cheats.cmd: awk '/^>/ {if (seq) print seq; print; seq = ""; next} {seq = seq $0} END {print seq}' {{file.fasta}}

cheats.title: Find which sequences contain a motif
cheats.cmd: awk '/^>/ {if (seq ~ m) print name; name = substr($1, 2); seq = ""; next} {seq = seq toupper($0)} END {if (seq ~ m) print name}' m={{motif:GAATTC}} {{file.fasta}}
cheats.notes: Works across line breaks. The motif can be a regex, e.g. GA[AT]TTC

cheats.title: Split a multi-FASTA into one file each
Get a region from a genome
cheats.notes: First run creates genome.fa.fai

cheats.title: Count mapped reads
cheats.notes: -F 4 skips unmapped. Add -q 30 for MAPQ ≥ 30

cheats.title: Reads in a region
cheats.notes: Needs a sorted, indexed BAM

cheats.title: Total bases covered by a BED
Regions that overlap another BED
cheats.notes: -v instead of -u = regions with no overlap

cheats.title: Only gene lines from a GTF
All gene names in a GTF
Quick stats for FASTA/FASTQ files
cheats.notes: Install with  conda install -c bioconda seqkit

cheats.title: Read QC report
cheats.cmd: mkdir -p qc && fastqc -t {{threads:4}} -o qc {{files:*.fastq.gz}} && multiqc qc -o qc
